questions.q: Explain the significance of India's location and its Standard Meridian.

answer.text: India occupies a central position on the head of the Indian Ocean, the only ocean named after a country. This location placed India on the important sea routes linking Europe and Africa with the countries of East and South-East Asia, enabling trade and the spread of Indian culture, ideas and religions to distant lands.

India stretches through nearly thirty degrees of longitude, so the local time in the far east and far west would differ by about two hours. To avoid confusion, a single Standard Meridian at 82 degrees 30 minutes east, passing through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh, was chosen. The time along this meridian is taken as Indian Standard Time, which is five and a half hours ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.

answer: Thus India's location gave it strategic and commercial importance, while the Standard Meridian gives the whole country one uniform time.
